mechanism_narrative: A sustained period of low federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS <= 0.25%) signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances with FEDFUNDS <= 0.25%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 in a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5 percentage points over the prior three months signals improving labor market conditions, which typically precedes stronger corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE declines > 0.5pp in 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 in a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous acceleration in both labor market strength (PAYEMS growth) and consumer spending (RSAFS growth) signals a self-reinforcing economic expansion, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is only active when both conditions are met, as the combined effect is greater than the sum of individual effects.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 0.5% and RSAFS growth > 0.3% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS growth > 0.5% and RSAFS growth > 0.3% over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 in a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high unemployment (UNRATE > 8.0%), a stable or rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS >= 0.10%) signals insufficient monetary stimulus to support economic recovery, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE > 8.0% and FEDFUNDS >= 0.10%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 in a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals improving labor market conditions, which typically leads to higher consumer confidence and spending, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances with PAYEMS growth > 0.2% in the prior month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 in a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95.0 (index) over the prior month signals weakening manufacturing activity, which typically precedes lower corporate profits and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO < 95.0, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 in a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals robust consumer and housing demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days. The signal is only active when both series show acceleration, as the combined effect is greater than the sum of individual effects.
candidate_trigger: HOUST growth > 0.8% and RSAFS growth > 0.4% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where HOUST growth > 0.8% and RSAFS growth > 0.4% over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 in a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 96.0) and rising unemployment (UNRATE > 8.0%), the economy is in a contractionary phase, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO < 96.0 and UNRATE > 8.0%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 in a 3-year rolling window.
